methods.label: Common-altitude area comparisons
methods.explanation:
Area comparisons let us use both given ratios without finding any lengths. Write \([XYZ]\) for the area of triangle \(XYZ\), and let \(S=[ABC]>0\). Triangles with bases on the same line and a common opposite vertex have area ratios equal to their base ratios.

Since \(BT=4ET\), triangles with vertex \(A\) give \([ABT]=4[AET]\), and triangles with vertex \(C\) give \([BCT]=4[CET]\). Adding these relations and using \(E\in AC\), we obtain
\[
[ABT]+[BCT]
=4\bigl([AET]+[CET]\bigr)
=4[ACT].
\]
The three triangles \(ABT\), \(BCT\), and \(ACT\) partition \(ABC\). Therefore \(S=5[ACT]\), so \([ACT]=S/5\).

Now use \(AT=3DT\). Triangles \(ACT\) and \(DCT\) have bases \(AT\) and \(DT\) on the same line and common vertex \(C\), giving \([ACT]=3[DCT]\). Hence
\[
[ACD]=[ACT]+[DCT]
=\frac43[ACT]
=\frac{4S}{15}.
\]
It follows that \([ABD]=S-[ACD]=11S/15\). Finally, triangles \(ACD\) and \(ABD\) have a common altitude from \(A\) to \(BC\), so
\[
\frac{CD}{BD}
=\frac{[ACD]}{[ABD]}
=\frac{4S/15}{11S/15}
=\boxed{\frac{4}{11}},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).

methods.label: A parallel line creates two similarities
methods.explanation:
A line through \(T\) parallel to \(BC\) lets us connect the two given ratios to the same auxiliary segment. First convert the ratios to fractions of whole segments:
\[
\frac{AT}{AD}=\frac{3}{3+1}=\frac34,
\qquad
\frac{ET}{EB}=\frac{1}{4+1}=\frac15.
\]
Draw the parallel through \(T\) to \(BC\), meeting \(EC\) at \(P\). Because \(T\) is inside \(EB\), this intersection lies inside \(EC\).

Parallel lines give equal corresponding angles, so \(\triangle ETP\) and \(\triangle EBC\) are similar by two equal angles. Their corresponding sides give
\[
\frac{TP}{BC}=\frac{ET}{EB}=\frac15.
\]
Also, \(TP\parallel DC\), so \(\triangle ATP\) and \(\triangle ADC\) are similar by two equal angles. Therefore
\[
\frac{TP}{CD}=\frac{AT}{AD}=\frac34.
\]
Combining these relations eliminates \(TP\):
\[
\frac{CD}{BC}
=\frac{CD}{TP}\cdot\frac{TP}{BC}
=\frac43\cdot\frac15
=\frac{4}{15}.
\]
Since \(BD=BC-CD\), we have \(BD/BC=11/15\). Thus
\[
\frac{CD}{BD}
=\frac{4/15}{11/15}
=\boxed{\frac{4}{11}},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
